Submodules

news.admin module

Django admin configuration for the news application.

This module registers the application’s custom user, article, publisher, and newsletter models with the Django administration site.

The admin classes configure how each model is displayed, searched, filtered, and edited in the Django admin interface.

class news.admin.ArticleAdmin(model, admin_site)[source]

Bases: ModelAdmin

Configure the Django admin interface for articles.

This admin configuration determines which Article fields are displayed in the article list and provides filtering and search functionality.

Articles can be filtered according to approval status, Publisher, and creation date.

Administrators can search article records using the article title or article content.

Variables:

  • list_display (tuple) – Article fields displayed in the Django admin list view.

  • list_filter (tuple) – Article fields available as filters in the admin interface.

  • search_fields (tuple) – Article fields searched when using the Django admin search facility.

list_display = ('title', 'author', 'publisher', 'approved', 'created_at')
list_filter = ('approved', 'publisher', 'created_at')
property media
search_fields = ('title', 'content')
class news.admin.CustomUserAdmin(model, admin_site)[source]

Bases: UserAdmin

Configure the Django admin interface for custom users.

This class extends Django’s standard django.contrib.auth.admin.UserAdmin class to include fields required by the news application.

The additional fields allow an administrator to view the user’s role and Reader subscription information.

The admin list displays the username, email address, application role, and staff status.

Variables:

  • fieldsets (tuple) – Extends the standard Django user fieldsets with the news application role and subscription fields.

  • add_fieldsets (tuple) – Extends the standard user creation form with the application role and email address.

  • list_display (tuple) – Fields displayed in the Django admin user list.

add_fieldsets = ((None, {'classes': ('wide',), 'fields': ('username', 'usable_password', 'password1', 'password2')}), ('News application', {'fields': ('role', 'email')}))
fieldsets = ((None, {'fields': ('username', 'password')}), ('Personal info', {'fields': ('first_name', 'last_name', 'email')}), ('Permissions', {'fields': ('is_active', 'is_staff', 'is_superuser', 'groups', 'user_permissions')}), ('Important dates', {'fields': ('last_login', 'date_joined')}), ('News application', {'fields': ('role', 'subscriptions_publishers', 'subscriptions_journalists')}))
list_display = ('username', 'email', 'role', 'is_staff')
property media
class news.admin.NewsletterAdmin(model, admin_site)[source]

Bases: ModelAdmin

Configure the Django admin interface for newsletters.

The newsletter admin list displays the newsletter title, author, and creation date.

Administrators can search newsletters using the title or description.

Variables:

  • list_display (tuple) – Newsletter fields displayed in the Django admin list view.

  • search_fields (tuple) – Newsletter fields used when searching from the Django admin interface.

list_display = ('title', 'author', 'created_at')
property media
search_fields = ('title', 'description')
class news.admin.PublisherAdmin(model, admin_site)[source]

Bases: ModelAdmin

Configure the Django admin interface for Publishers.

Publisher records are displayed by name and can be searched by their Publisher name.

The normal application workflow allows Publisher accounts to manage their employees through the frontend. The Django admin interface is intended primarily for system maintenance.

Variables:

  • list_display (tuple) – Publisher fields displayed in the Django admin list.

  • search_fields (tuple) – Publisher fields searched by the Django admin search facility.

list_display = ('name',)
property media

news.serializers module

Serializers for the news REST API.

This module contains Django REST Framework serializers used to convert application model instances to and from JSON-compatible representations.

The serializers support the following models:

  • news.models.CustomUser

  • news.models.Publisher

  • news.models.Article

  • news.models.Newsletter

Validation is also performed for article approval and Publisher membership.

class news.serializers.ArticleSerializer(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: ModelSerializer

Serialize news articles.

The serializer provides the normal Article model fields together with convenient read-only representations of the author name and Publisher name.

It also performs validation for:

  • article approval

  • Publisher membership

Variables:

  • author_name (rest_framework.serializers.CharField) – Read-only username of the article author.

  • publisher_name (rest_framework.serializers.CharField) – Read-only name of the Publisher associated with the article.

validate_approved(approved)[source]

Validate changes to the article approval status.

The method checks whether the current authenticated user has Editor privileges when an article changes from unapproved to approved.

Superusers are also permitted to approve articles.

If the approval value is not changing from False to True, the value is returned without an Editor check.

Parameters:

approved (bool) – The proposed approval value for the article.

Returns:

The validated approval value.

Return type:

bool

Raises:

serializers.ValidationError – If a non-Editor attempts to approve an article.

validate_publisher(publisher)[source]

Validate the selected Publisher.

Journalists may only assign an article to a Publisher for which they are registered as a Journalist.

Editors and superusers are permitted to work with Publisher articles without this Journalist membership check.

A None Publisher value is valid because an article may instead be an independent Journalist article.

Parameters:

publisher (Publisher) – The Publisher selected for the article.

Returns:

The validated Publisher instance, or None for an independent Journalist article.

Return type:

Publisher or None

Raises:

serializers.ValidationError – If a Journalist attempts to use a Publisher that they do not belong to.

class news.serializers.NewsletterSerializer(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: ModelSerializer

Serialize newsletters.

The serializer exposes Newsletter details together with a read-only representation of the author’s username.

Articles associated with the Newsletter are represented through the Newsletter model’s many-to-many relationship.

Variables:

author_name (rest_framework.serializers.CharField) – Read-only username of the Newsletter author.

class news.serializers.PublisherSerializer(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: ModelSerializer

Serialize Publisher records.

This serializer exposes Publisher information as well as the Editors and Journalists associated with the Publisher.

The Publisher ID and creation date are read-only.

class news.serializers.UserSerializer(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: ModelSerializer

Serialize application users.

This serializer exposes basic user information, the application role, and Reader subscriptions.

The user’s ID and role are read-only through this serializer.
